featured_reviews.name: Ruchit Barodia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Earth Café, Churchgate feels like a quiet pause button in the middle of Mumbai’s relentless rhythm. Tucked away yet perfectly placed, this café welcomes you with an earthy charm that instantly soothes the senses. The moment you step in, you’re greeted by a calming blend of natural tones, soft lighting, and a thoughtfully curated space that feels both modern and grounded—true to its name.

The ambience strikes a beautiful balance between cozy and classy, making it ideal for everything from relaxed conversations to peaceful solo time. Whether you’re catching up with a friend, working on your laptop, or simply enjoying a slow meal, Earth Café creates an atmosphere that encourages you to linger a little longer.

The food is where the café truly shines. Every dish feels fresh, wholesome, and crafted with care. From vibrant salads and nourishing bowls to indulgent yet guilt-free desserts, the menu caters wonderfully to health-conscious diners without compromising on taste. The beverages—especially their coffees and refreshing coolers—are well-balanced and thoughtfully prepared, making them perfect companions to the food.

What stands out most is the attention to detail: warm service, beautifully plated dishes, and a sense of calm that’s rare in the heart of South Mumbai. Earth Café isn’t just a place to eat; it’s an experience—one that leaves you feeling lighter, happier, and eager to return.

A true gem at Churchgate, perfect for those who appreciate good food, serene vibes, and mindful living.

featured_reviews.name: Rajeev Rao
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this café in Churchgate on a Sunday afternoon and unfortunately, the experience was quite disappointing. We walked in and ordered a tiramisu, an opera slice, and an iced café latte. The waitress also recommended their special Ube iced latte, which we decided to try.

The coffee was honestly the biggest letdown. The Ube latte had a very strange, nutty flavor and tasted nothing like a latte. We really didn’t enjoy it. To their credit, the staff handled the feedback well and removed the coffee from the bill.

The desserts weren’t much better. The opera slice tasted cold and not fresh at all. We had originally wanted a walnut cake, but it wasn’t available. The tiramisu was overly bitter with a very strong coffee flavor — it lacked the balanced sweetness and creamy texture you’d normally expect from a tiramisu, and instead tasted more like a coffee-flavored dessert.

Overall, all three items we tried were below average, which was surprising considering the location and reputation of the place. The ambiance was decent and the service was polite, but the food and drinks were disappointing enough that I wouldn’t recommend it.

featured_reviews.review_text:
It is with considerable disappointment that I write regarding my visit to Starbucks, Churchgate, this afternoon.
I ordered two Grande Iced Brown Sugar Oatmilk , and I regret to say the drinks bore little resemblance to what they ought to be. Both were remarkably thin and watery, wholly lacking the body, richness, and balance one expects from this particular beverage. When I raised the matter with the server, I was told the drink was simply "low calorie." I explained that this did not account for how diluted it tasted, and requested something better prepared. Her remedy was merely to add sugar to sweeten it and that, apparently, was the improved version.
I have patronised Starbucks outlets across the city for years and have never encountered anything of this sort. At this price a cup, this falls well short of the standard the brand has long stood for. I am left genuinely puzzled as to whether the decline is one of process, of ingredients, or simply of the care taken by whoever prepared the drink.
I do hope this is brought to the attention of the store, as the experience was decidedly beneath what Starbucks represents.

featured_reviews.name: Sadanand Rawool
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have visited Starbucks many times, both in India and abroad, but this was easily one of the worst experiences I’ve ever had.

The staff was extremely rude and completely unhelpful. They didn’t try to understand my concern and instead kept talking among themselves rather than assisting me properly.

I had a CRED coupon worth ₹300 that was about to expire in 4 days. I’ve used similar coupons before at other outlets without any issues, so this wasn’t new to me. However, the staff here claimed they were not aware of such coupons. They then insisted that I had to purchase additional food or beverages along with my coffee in order to use it, which is not how the coupon works.

Frustrated, I decided to leave and went to another store to use the coupon only to find that it had already been marked as used. I immediately returned to this outlet to clarify, since I hadn’t made any purchase. Instead of helping, they simply said they “don’t know anything” and that the coupon was already entered into the system and expired, offering no explanation or solution.

This kind of careless handling and lack of accountability is unacceptable. The rude behavior, poor communication, and complete disregard for customer concerns made an already bad situation worse.

Truly a pathetic experience that completely ruined my day.

With natural light pouring in, wooden accents, and an almost meditative vibe, the ambiance lives up to the name “Zen.”

The menu leans towards healthy, vegetarian fare with Mediterranean and global influences. Their open sandwiches, hummus plates, and freshly baked goods are flavorful and light. featured_reviews.name: Arin Paul
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Markiv’s feels like a café that knows exactly what it wants to be and stays within that comfort zone. It offers a fairly extensive menu of continental and café-style dishes, presented neatly and priced in the mid-range for the area.

We tried the Americano, Peach Iced Tea, Grilled Chicken Risotto, and Chicken Markiv’s.

The Americano was straightforward and clean, no bitterness, no complexity. It does what an Americano is expected to do, without leaving a strong impression either way. The Peach Iced Tea was refreshing and mildly sweet, pleasant enough for Mumbai weather, though not particularly memorable.

The Chicken Risotto was decent. Creamy, adequately cooked, and comforting, but lacked depth or a distinct flavour punch. It felt safe rather than inspired. A good option if you’re in the mood for something mild and filling, but not something you’d crave or remember later.

The Chicken Markiv’s, which appears to be one of their signature dishes, was served well and plated nicely. The chicken was tender and paired with mashed potatoes and vegetables. Again, the flavours were balanced and acceptable, but it didn’t rise above being just fine. Nothing was wrong with the dish, but nothing truly stood out either.

The menu itself is broad, covering pizzas, burgers, pasta, risottos, rice plates, and main course options, both vegetarian and non-vegetarian. It caters well to mixed groups with varied preferences. Portions are reasonable, and pricing is what you’d expect from a café of this type.

Service was polite and timely, without being overly warm or inattentive. The ambience is comfortable and casual, suitable for conversations, short meetings, or a relaxed meal, though it doesn’t have a distinct character that sets it apart from similar cafés.

Overall, Cafe Markiv’s is reliable but unremarkable. Nothing great, nothing bad. It’s a decent place if you’re nearby and want a predictable café meal without surprises. Not a destination café, but functional and consistent for what it offers.

featured_reviews.name: kalyani auti
featured_reviews.review_text: Very tasty food! We had Aubergine Teriyaki, Pepperoni Pizza, Fresh Lime Soda, Rosemary Fennel Lemonade and Chocolate Profiterole. The Aubergine Teriyaki is a must try! Amazing flavors with the nice texture of aubergine and black rice. The Rosemary Fennel Lemonade tasted amazing with it. The ambience is also good, nice jazz music. Good service as well.

featured_reviews.name: Suraj Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Kala Ghoda Cafe during the Kala Ghoda Festival with friends, and what a find this place turned out to be. Tucked away inside a small lane, it’s a little difficult to spot. After the madness of the fest, this café felt like a lake in a desert, felt calm, comforting, and exactly what we needed.
The vibe is warm and lively at the same time, with a charming setup and even a hidden bar counter that adds to the character of the place.
Coming to the food and drinks, they are the absolute winners. I tried the Masala Cappuccino, and it was truly unique, with a lovely kick of masala chai flavours blended into the coffee. Something I’ve never had before and surprisingly addictive.
The Cheese Chilli Toast, recommended by the waiter, did not disappoint—super cheesy with perfectly crispy bread. The Cottage Cheese Burger was honestly to die for, easily one of the best vegetarian burgers I’ve had—flavourful, filling, and perfectly balanced.
And the real star of the show was the Hash Brown dish “Rosti, crispy on the outside, creamy on the inside, and just cooked to perfection. Absolute comfort food.
Overall, great food, lovely coffee, welcoming vibes, and a peaceful break from the festival rush. Kala Ghoda Cafe is definitely a place I’d keep coming back to.

featured_reviews.name: Diya D'Sa
featured_reviews.review_text: Cozy ambiance and great service! The server recommended the chili cheese toast and it did not disappoint—perfectly crisp, cheesy, and with the right amount of spice. The waffle was good as well, though it came with quite a bit of nuts, granola, and raisins (great if you enjoy that). With the fresh fruit, I didn’t even need the syrup. My favorites were definitely the cheese toast and the chai. I also picked up a bag of their coffee beans, which are perfect for making coffee at home or even garnishing espresso martinis.

featured_reviews.name: Paras Mhatre
featured_reviews.review_text: Kala Ghoda Café in Fort makes for a memorable stop. Service was decent, though it could be sharper. The food hit the right notes—the mushroom black rice risotto was warm and comforting, the four-cheese pizza hearty and fulfilling, and the carrot dish pleasantly fine. What truly elevates the experience is the café’s vibe and ambiance, which are simply noteworthy. Overall, a good outing worth revisiting!!!!!

featured_reviews.review_text: A true gem in the fort, this place consistently enchants me with every visit. 💖 Both the bar and cafe sections hold a unique charm. featured_reviews.name: Indrayudh Roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
If it could be described for those of you looking for a one -liner it has the 1970s charm. Take yourself back to a time and place that was slower and more intentional. When you think you have had to get away from the working life it becomes that the mirrors are symbols that show up and do not hesitate to amplify your experience. It is not just the variety and care of the beer that is on offer it is the fact that you will be able to combat the courage inside of you. Once you see that there is no stopping it you will be able to understand why such a curiosity resides amongst the modern crowd of buildings and overpriced places that are mainly to do with neoliberalism being on its last legs of defeat.

Anyway once you have a couple drinks here you will forget about anything to do with that and you will surely enjoy. It is quiet and serene broken only by the passerby that is sure to inquire if they could enter and have themselves entertained. The main attraction is how you get to be in an atmosphere that is ambient and lowkey but without the busyness of everyday.

So you think you can get a better idea from pictures than a review that's. . also fine. But there thing is you might want to understand why this place carries their selection rather than being beholden to the ability of carrying whatever else there is out there. We can understand this by the fact that it is always going to be a present fact without the intervention of that which is considered most unlikely.

Unlikeness. Unlikeness.

That being the keyword one should always understand that the service can be improved.

It should do justice to the legacy of the place as a drinking house where their is nostalgia and modernism in equal measure. It is not enough to sell you the tagline but they must be able to convince you that you were at the right place at the right time.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Really disappointed with the service at the Nariman Point outlet — and this is not the first time. The barista named Madhavi was unnecessarily rude and behaved as if taking an order was a favour to the customer. There was no warmth, no basic courtesy, and zero effort to make the experience pleasant.

For a brand that positions itself as a premium coffee chain, the attitude here feels the opposite of hospitality. On top of that, the lack of alternative milk options is surprising in 2026 — most cafés understand that customers have dietary preferences today.

What stands out even more is how different this feels compared to Starbucks, where staff are trained to be polite, welcoming, and customer-focused regardless of rush or mood. Coffee quality matters, but service is what makes people return.

I hope management seriously looks into staff behaviour and customer experience at this outlet — because right now, it’s pushing customers away rather than building loyalty.

The Iconic Dosas & Idlis: The Ghee Podi Idli was cloud-soft, drenched in flavorful ghee, and packed a perfect spicy punch with the podi. The Benne Butter Masala Dosa was perfectly crisp on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and rich in flavor.
The Chutneys: A special shoutout to their signature chutneys—fresh, vibrant, and the perfect accompaniment to the main dishes.
The Grand Finale: You cannot leave this place without trying their Coffee Ice Cream. It is an absolute game-changer! It perfectly captures the rich, bold, and aromatic essence of traditional filter coffee but in a creamy, refreshing frozen dessert. It’s not overly sweet, making it the ultimate treat for true coffee lovers.
The service was incredibly fast despite the bustling crowd, and the quality of ingredients truly shines through in every bite.

Verdict: Exceptional food, vibrant vibes, and a 10/10 experience. Whether you are going for a heavy breakfast or a sweet evening treat, this place never disappoints. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Tarun Joseph
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Rameshwaram Cafe at Churchgate this morning for a quick breakfast like old times.
I’m a Kannadiga and I've lived in Bengaluru for a couple of years and used to visit Rameshwaram Cafe (Indiranagar and JP Nagar outlets), at least once a month. Even now, whenever I go back to Bengaluru, it’s a mandatory stop. So when they announced they were opening in Mumbai, I was genuinely excited. I’ve been missing proper dosa and idli here.

But what I ate today was not Rameshwaram Cafe.

I ordered my usual ghee pudi plain dosa and there was barely any pudi on it. The taste was completely off. It didn’t have the flavour, the texture, or even the smell that makes Rameshwaram Cafe what it is. The taste just felt different, very different. It honestly didn’t even feel like the Rameshwaram Cafe I remember from Bengaluru.
I didn’t try the pudi idli myself, but my friends ordered it and said it was just average as well.

After all the hype, the long queues, and the name they’ve built in Bengaluru, this was unbelievably disappointing. If this is what Rameshwaram Cafe Mumbai is serving, they’re just riding on the Bengaluru brand while delivering something far below that standard.

A truly mediocre experience. If you’ve actually eaten at the Bengaluru outlet, this will feel like a huge downgrade.

featured_reviews.name: Moumita Roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had the chance to visit Leopold Cafe and it truly feels like stepping into a piece of Mumbai’s history. Established in 1871, this iconic cafe carries a legacy that you can sense the moment you walk in—right from its vintage interiors to the buzzing, old-school charm.  ￼

The atmosphere is lively, slightly chaotic in the best way, and filled with a mix of locals and tourists from around the world. The walls, adorned with memorabilia and stories from the past, give the place a unique character that goes beyond just food.  ￼

The menu is extensive, offering everything from Indian to continental and Chinese dishes. The food is tasty and comforting, with generous portions, but the real highlight is enjoying a relaxed meal with a chilled drink while soaking in the vibrant Colaba vibe.  ￼

That said, it does get quite crowded, and you might have to wait for a table. Service can feel a bit rushed during peak hours, which is understandable given how popular the place is.  ￼

Overall, Leopold Cafe is less about fine dining and more about the experience, history, and atmosphere. It’s one of those places you visit not just for the food, but to truly feel the spirit of Mumbai. Definitely worth a visit at least once!

featured_reviews.name: Rachit Chandra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Leopold Cafe is one of Mumbai’s most iconic and historic cafés, known not just for its food but also for its deep connection with the city’s past. One of the most striking and emotional aspects of the place is that the gunshot marks from the 26/11 terror attack are still preserved, making it a powerful reminder of history and resilience.

The food and drinks are good in taste and reasonably priced compared to the location and popularity of the café. They offer a wide variety of options, including Indian, Continental, Chinese food, snacks, and beverages, making it suitable for all kinds of visitors. Portions are decent, and service is fairly quick considering the crowd.

The café is extremely crowded on weekends, especially in the evenings, so you may have to wait for a table. The atmosphere is lively, vibrant, and full of energy, attracting tourists, locals, and international visitors alike. The staff manages the crowd well and remains polite despite the rush.

Located in Colaba, it’s very close to major attractions like Gateway of India and is easy to reach. Overall, Leopold Cafe is a must-visit place in Mumbai for its history, legacy, lively vibe, and value-for-money food. A place you should experience at least once.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Third Wave Coffee, Thakur Complex – Late Nights Done Right

Some places are built for brunch.
This one? Built for 11:30 PM conversations that accidentally stretch into the night.

We dropped by Third Wave Coffee at Thakur Complex close to midnight, and the biggest win right away it’s 24/7. In a city where most cafés shut just when you start craving coffee, this already puts it ahead of the curve.

📍 Location & Accessibility

Right off the main road in Thakur Complex, so no hunting through lanes or Google Maps confusion.

Easy to reach

Easy to spot

And more importantly easy to rely on, even late at night

☕ Coffee & Drinks – Mostly Hits, One Miss

We tried:

Vietnamese Matcha

French Vanilla Latte

Hot Chocolate

Sea Salt Mocha

Verdict?

Vietnamese Matcha – unique, well-balanced, not overly sweet

Hot Chocolate – comforting, smooth, exactly what you expect

Sea Salt Mocha – standout; that sweet-salty balance hits just right

Only slight miss:

French Vanilla Latte – lacked sweetness, felt a bit underwhelming compared to the rest
🥪 Food – Solid Support Cast

Paneer Tikka Sandwich – flavourful, satisfying

Mexican Masala Sandwich – nicely spiced, works well with coffee

Nothing experimental but well executed and dependable, which is exactly what you want in a café setting.

🪑 Ambience & Vibe

Clean, warm lighting, and that familiar café energy where:

Some people are working

Some are catching up

Some are just unwinding after a long day

Late at night, it feels even better less noise, more vibe.
📊 SGT Decision Scorecard

Parameter	Score	Insight

Accessibility	9/10	Prime location, easy entry
Experience Quality	8/10	Strong drinks, good food
Consistency	8/10	Mostly on point
Value for Money	8/10	Worth it for the overall experience

🎯 Reality Verdict

✅ Go for: Late-night coffee runs, casual meetups, reliable café experience

⚠️ Be aware: Some drinks may need slight tweaking (like sweetness levels)

💎 Best use case: When the city is shutting down, but you’re not

🧾 Final Take

Third Wave Coffee here isn’t trying to be fancy it’s trying to be reliable, accessible, and consistently good.

And honestly? It succeeds.

Because sometimes, the best café isn’t the one with the best coffee
it’s the one that’s open when you need it, and delivers when you show up.

This place is an exciting yet relaxing haven for foodies!
And the service and behaviour of the staff and management is truly courteous and welcoming!

featured_reviews.name: ANIL ZALA
featured_reviews.review_text:
This café truly feels like a perfect little escape from the rush of everyday life—a place where you can slow down, breathe, and simply enjoy the moment. It’s the kind of spot that naturally draws you in, whether you’re looking to unwind after a long day, meet up with friends for a casual catch-up, or even spend some quiet time by yourself with a warm cup of coffee. From the moment you walk in, there’s a comforting charm that makes you want to stay a little longer than planned.

One of the best things about this place is how effortlessly it brings people together. It’s ideal for friendly conversations, laughter-filled meetups, and those unplanned chats that somehow turn into cherished memories. The seating arrangement feels thoughtfully designed, offering enough privacy to have meaningful conversations while still maintaining a lively, welcoming atmosphere. Whether you’re sitting across from a close friend, sharing stories and laughter, or simply enjoying a relaxed conversation over coffee, the space encourages connection in the most natural way.

The ambience plays a huge role in making this café so inviting. Warm lighting, tasteful décor, and soft, gentle music come together to create an environment that feels calm yet uplifting. The music is perfectly balanced—not too loud, not too quiet—allowing conversations to flow without interruption. It adds a subtle rhythm to the space, enhancing the overall experience without ever overpowering it. The cozy vibes instantly put you at ease, making it a great place to relax and unwind.

This café is also well-suited for quick bites, making it a convenient stop whether you’re in a hurry or simply craving something light to go with your coffee. The menu complements the atmosphere perfectly, offering snacks that are easy to enjoy while chatting or working. It’s the kind of place where you can comfortably order something small, sip your drink slowly, and still feel completely satisfied.

What truly sets this spot apart is the way time seems to slow down once you’re there. There’s no pressure to rush, no sense of being hurried out. Each sip of coffee feels comforting and just right, encouraging you to pause and enjoy the present moment. It’s easy to lose track of time as conversations stretch on, laughter fills the air, and the outside world fades into the background.

This café is more than just a place to grab a drink—it’s a space where moments are created. It’s where casual meetups turn into long conversations, and simple coffee breaks become meaningful experiences. Whether you’re catching up with old friends, meeting someone new, or just enjoying your own company, the atmosphere makes every visit feel special.

In essence, this is a place that blends comfort, warmth, and simplicity beautifully. With its inviting ambience, relaxed vibe, and perfect balance of music and conversation, it offers an experience that goes beyond just coffee. It’s a cozy haven where memories are made, connections are strengthened, and every visit leaves you feeling refreshed and content. ☕✨

featured_reviews.name: Kapil Jaiswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Aroma Cafe at The Hive once again, this time with friends, and it reminded us why we were happy to come back. Some places make a good first impression, but only a repeat visit tells you whether they truly maintain their standards. Aroma Cafe did exactly that—with good food, warm hospitality, and a vibe that instantly makes you feel relaxed.
The moment you walk in, the atmosphere feels bright, comfortable, and welcoming. It has that perfect café energy where you can sit for long conversations without feeling rushed. The interiors are pleasant, the seating is comfortable, and the overall ambience carries genuinely good vibes. Whether you’re meeting friends, working for a while, or just taking a break, the place feels easy and enjoyable.
What stood out once again was the hospitality. The staff were polite, attentive, and quick to help whenever needed. They were warm in their interactions and handled the service smoothly, which made our group outing even better. Good hospitality often defines the overall memory of a place, and Aroma Cafe gets this part right.
We ordered quite a spread so everyone could try something different, and the meal turned out to be both satisfying and enjoyable.
Creole Potatoes
A great starter with crispy potatoes tossed in flavourful seasoning. Nicely spiced, crunchy outside, and soft inside—perfect for sharing with friends.
Iced Cold Coffee
Refreshing, smooth, and nicely chilled. It had the right balance of coffee flavour and sweetness, making it ideal for a casual café outing.
Nutella Hot Chocolate
Rich, indulgent, and comforting. The Nutella gave it a creamy hazelnut twist that made it feel more special than a regular hot chocolate.
Veg Alfredo Pasta (Penne) with Extra Cheese Sauce
Creamy, filling, and comforting in every bite. The penne was cooked well, and the extra cheese sauce made it richer and more satisfying.
Coconut Matcha Cloud
A unique and refreshing drink with an interesting flavour combination. The coconut added smoothness while the matcha gave it a light earthy finish.
Mango Smoothie Bowl
Fresh, colourful, and enjoyable. The mango flavour was bright and naturally sweet, making it a lighter and healthier option on the table.
Creamy Garlic Mushroom
Full of flavour and very well prepared. The mushrooms were cooked nicely in a creamy garlic base that was rich without feeling too heavy.
Cheesy Garlic Bread
Warm, cheesy, and hard to resist. Crisp edges with soft bread inside, topped with enough cheese and garlic flavour to make it a crowd favourite.

Veg Spaghetti Aglio Olio Pasta
Simple yet flavourful. The garlic and olive oil coating was balanced, and the spaghetti had a clean, satisfying taste.
What we appreciated most was that despite ordering many different items, the quality remained consistent across the table. Portions were good, presentation was neat, and everything arrived at a comfortable pace. Nothing felt rushed, and we could enjoy the meal while catching up properly.
Another strong point is how suitable the café is for conversations. Some places are either too loud or too formal, but Aroma Cafe strikes a very good middle ground. It feels lively yet peaceful enough to talk comfortably, which is exactly what you want during a friends’ outing.
Cleanliness and upkeep were also impressive. The tables were maintained well, the service area looked organised, and the overall environment felt managed with care.
A repeat visit often comes with higher expectations, and Aroma Cafe lived up to them. Good food, pleasant ambience, and warm service came together once again to create a very enjoyable experience.
Overall, Aroma Cafe at The Hive continues to be a dependable and welcoming place for coffee, comfort food, and quality time with friends. With its good vibes, great hospitality, and consistent food quality, it remains a café we’d happily visit again. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a relaxed and enjoyable café experience.
